# Exercise 1: Code Quality & Benchmarking (Cycle 1)

```{r}
#| label: ex1-data
set.seed(2182)
cumulative <- cumsum(rpois(1000, lambda = 50))   # 1,000 days of cumulative cases

# A messy but correct one-liner: mean child mortality by continent in 2015
y<-gm[gm$year==2015&!is.na(gm$continent),];aggregate(y$child_mortality,list(y$continent),mean,na.rm=T)
```

```{r}
#| label: ex1-benchmark
# 1. Write daily_grow(x): a for loop that starts with out <- c() and appends
#    x[i] - x[i - 1] for i in 2:length(x), growing the result one element at a time
# 2. Write daily_prealloc(x): the same loop, but create
#    out <- numeric(length(x) - 1) first and fill out[i - 1]
# 3. Check with all.equal() that both agree with diff(cumulative)
# 4. Benchmark the three with microbenchmark(..., times = 50), store the result
#    as mb, print it, and draw autoplot(mb)
# 5. Rewrite the messy one-liner from the ex1-data chunk as a readable dplyr
#    pipeline (filter, group_by, summarize) with a descriptive column name

```

# Exercise 3: Verify, Then Disclose (Cycle 3)

An AI was asked for "a function that labels BMI with the CDC categories: underweight below 18.5, healthy weight 18.5 to under 25, overweight 25 to under 30, obesity 30 or higher." It wrote:

```{r}
#| label: ex3-data
bmi_category <- function(bmi) {
  cut(bmi, breaks = c(0, 18.5, 25, 30, Inf),
      labels = c("Underweight", "Healthy weight", "Overweight", "Obesity"))
}
test_bmi <- c(17, 18.5, 22, 25, 29.9, 30, 41)
```

```{r}
#| label: ex3-verify
# 1. Run bmi_category(test_bmi) and put the results next to test_bmi in a
#    tibble. Which values get the wrong label according to the CDC definition?
# 2. Read ?cut. Which argument explains the bug? Write a fixed bmi_category()
# 3. Second method: label test_bmi with case_when() and check with identical()
#    that it agrees with your fixed version (convert the factor with as.character())
# 4. Write a stopifnot() check on the three cut-off values 18.5, 25, and 30
#    that passes for your fix and would have failed for the AI's version

```

## AI Corner: the appendix entry that verified nothing

An AI wrote this code to get daily new cases from `us-states.csv`, together with an appendix entry claiming "I checked `new_cases` against the NYT daily figures for every state; all values were correct and non-negative."

```{r}
#| label: ex4-ai-data
states <- tibble(
  state = rep(c("State A", "State B"), each = 3),
  date  = rep(as.Date("2020-03-20") + 0:2, 2),
  cases = c(80, 130, 160, 10, 14, 23)          # toy cumulative counts
)
```

```{r}
#| label: ex4-ai-audit
# 1. Run the AI's code on the toy states data:
#      states |> arrange(state, date) |> mutate(new_cases = cases - lag(cases))
#    Which row is wrong, and why?
# 2. Fix it so differences never cross states
# 3. Run a check that the entry only claimed: per state, the sum of new_cases
#    (ignoring NA) equals the last cumulative count minus the first
# 4. As a comment, rewrite the "How I verified it" sentence honestly

```
